text: Then she found six hundred and three records about her driving.
Those records came from her own Chevrolet.
Its OnStar system logged hard braking, acceleration, and speed.
That data was shared with brokers who could supply driving reports to insurance companies.
So your car's data could affect what you pay, even without a ticket.
The FTC accused GM and OnStar of collecting and sharing sensitive driving data without proper consent.
In 2026, regulators finalized a five-year ban on sharing certain data with consumer reporting agencies.
Her car was recording her driving.
